_meta.title: Identity & Directory Attacks
_meta.description: The modern crown-jewel domain: Active Directory, Kerberos, NTLM, and enterprise SSO. Where enterprises actually fall. Every technique here is documented in public certification curricula and mapped to its defensive control.

techniques.name: Kerberoasting
techniques.summary: Request service tickets (TGS) for accounts with SPNs; the ticket is encrypted with the service account's NTLM hash, so it can be cracked offline at leisure. No admin rights needed to request tickets - any domain user can enumerate and roast. Weak service-account passwords fall in minutes.

detection.description: Windows EID 4769 with RC4 (0x17) encryption and no 4768 in the same session; abnormal volume of TGS requests from a single principal in a short window; RC4 tickets are themselves legacy-flagged.
mitigations: 25+ character random passwords on all service accounts, or gMSA (group Managed Service Accounts)
Disable RC4 where possible; enforce AES
Alert on 4769 RC4 request bursts; tiered admin model keeps service accounts out of Domain Admins

techniques.name: AS-REP Roasting
techniques.summary: Accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' return an AS-REP encrypted with the user's own key to anyone who asks - offline crackable, no credentials needed at all. The misconfiguration is older-domain legacy and quiet, so enumeration finds surprises.

detection.description: EID 4768 with pre-auth type 0 (no preauth); volume of AS requests against accounts that normally never authenticate interactively; hashcat-mode 18200 activity indicators from EDR on endpoints.
mitigations: Audit and clear the UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH flag - it should be false on every account
Strong passphrases / gMSA as backstop
Alert on 4768 preauth-missing events

techniques.name: Pass-the-Hash / Pass-the-Ticket
techniques.summary: Replay stolen credential material without ever knowing the password: NTLM hash passed directly to authentication, or a captured Kerberos ticket injected into a new session. Lateral movement with zero credential cracking - the reason credential theft beats password attacks in real engagements.

detection.description: EID 4624 logon type 3 (network) with NTLM where host normally uses Kerberos; ticket reuse across hosts within a ticket lifetime (same logon ID, different source machines); abnormal NTLM traffic between workstations (workstation-to-workstation NTLM is nearly always lateral movement).
mitigations: Credential Guard (isolates LSASS secrets via virtualization)
Tiered admin model - admin credentials never touch non-tier-0 hosts
Restricted Admin Mode / Remote Credential Guard for RDP
Disable NTLM where feasible; else NTLM auditing and SMB signing

techniques.name: DCSync Replication Abuse
techniques.summary: Hold 'Replicating Directory Changes' rights (or steal a DC's trust) and ask a domain controller to replicate password hashes directly - every account in the domain, including krbtgt. The endgame move: with krbtgt's hash you forge golden tickets. Treat as game-over, not a checkpoint.

detection.description: EID 4662 'Replicating Directory Changes' access by non-DC principals; replication attempts to member workstations; Get-ReplicationChanges API calls from unexpected sources. DC-to-workstation replication is a definitive alert.
mitigations: Audit 'Replicating Directory Changes' ACEs - only DCs and sanctioned tools should hold them
Tier 0 isolation for DCs (no interactive logon by non-DC admins)
After compromise: krbtgt password reset TWICE (the interval rule) - and plan for it in IR

techniques.name: Golden / Silver Ticket Forgery
techniques.summary: With krbtgt's NTLM hash, mint offline-valid TGTs for any identity, any group, ten-year lifetime - golden tickets that outlive the compromise that created them. Silver tickets (service-account hash) forge TGS for one service with no DC contact at all, making them quieter and harder to correlate.

detection.description: Ticket anomalies: lifetime violations, missing PAC, or PAC signature mismatches; EID 4769 requests for services with no prior 4768 TGT issuance; tickets referencing accounts with no corresponding domain activity. Full detection is hard - the durability of the artifact is the point.
mitigations: Protect krbtgt hash: tier-0 hygiene, DCSync defense, dual krbtgt password rotation post-incident
Restrict service-account privilege; any account whose hash is stolen silvers only that one service
PAC signature validation and ticket-lifetime anomaly tooling (e.g. defcon/BlueHive-class log analysis)

techniques.name: NTLM Relay (incl. ESC8 Web Enrollment)
techniques.summary: Relay an authenticated NTLM handshake to another service that accepts it: coerce a machine to authenticate to the attacker (Printerbug, PetitPotam) and forward to LDAP/SMB/AD-CS web enrollment. Signing/sealing (SMB, LDAP) blocks it; plain HTTP endpoints (AD CS CertSrv) do not, which is why ESC8 became the modern kill chain's favorite door.

detection.description: Coercion indicators: machine-triggered authentication to unusual hosts (EID 4625/4776 correlation, MS-EFSR/MS-RPRN calls logged via Sysmon EID 3 to non-standard destinations); relay signatures: NTLM auth to ADCS/LDAP from a workstation address that should never do so.
mitigations: Enable SMB and LDAP signing/sealing everywhere (the fundamental fix)
Disable NTLM entirely or restrict to explicit allowlist; disable ADCS HTTP enrollment or require Kerberos/EPA
Patch coercion vectors (PetitPotam fix) and disable Print Spooler on servers not needing it
Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA) on AD CS

techniques.name: AD CS Misconfiguration Abuse (ESC1-ESC8)
techniques.summary: Certificate templates misconfigured (ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT, low-ACL enrollment, manager-approval gaps, HTTP-only enrollment) let any domain user mint certificates impersonating privileged principals - authentication that bypasses password policy entirely and leaves no NTLM/LM artifacts.

detection.description: Certification Authority audit (EID 4887/4899) showing enrollment for privileged templates from non-privileged callers; issued certificates with SAN mismatches; Certipy/Locksmith-style audit tooling run on a schedule is itself the primary defense because detection in-flight is weak.
mitigations: Run Locksmith / PSPKIAudit - remediate template ACLs and flag settings (ESC1-8 checklist is now a standard hardening task)
Disable ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT unless a template truly requires it
Enforce manager approval + authorized signatures on high-privilege templates
Kill HTTP enrollment (EPA required) - closes ESC8 and the relay kill chain together

techniques.name: ACL & Delegation Abuse (BloodHound Paths)
techniques.summary: Enterprise AD is a graph of forgotten permissions: GenericAll on a user (shadow credential / target kerberoast), WriteDacl on a group, DCSync rights on an OU, unconstrained or resource-based constrained delegation letting a machine impersonate anyone to a target service. BloodHound made these paths computable - which cuts both ways, and the defensive use is the same tool.

detection.description: EID 5136 (directory object changes) on privileged objects; new SPNs set on accounts (delegation staging); certificate-based shadow-credential activity (EID 4887 msDS-KeyCredentialLink writes);BloodHound collection itself is visible - SharpHound sessions from non-audit hosts should alert.
mitigations: BloodHound run defensively on a schedule - find your own attack paths before they do
Strip unsanctioned ACEs from tier-0 objects; tiered admin model
Restrict delegation: no unconstrained delegation outside cluster needs, RBCD scoping documented
EID 5136 auditing on privileged containers

techniques.name: Password Spraying & Credential Stuffing
techniques.summary: The anti-pattern of brute force: one or two very common passwords rotated across many usernames (spraying), or replaying breach-corpus credential pairs (stuffing). Auth failures blend into baseline noise, so the move trades loudness per account for breadth across accounts - which is also exactly the shape defenders hunt for. Noisy-but-recoverable by doctrine; the blast lands as account lockouts and alert fatigue.

detection.description: Breadth-over-rate heuristic: single source IP/session generating EID 4625/4771 failures across MANY distinct accounts is spraying, even at low rate; lockout spikes (EID 4740) cluster downstream; Entra ID sign-in risk detections and breach-password match telemetry flag stuffing at cloud IdPs; watch for distributed-source sprays via fail2ban-style correlation and geovelocity anomalies.
mitigations: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) - renders stolen passwords inert
Smart lockout that splits per-user and per-source thresholds (avoids the lockout-DoS side effect)
Breached-password screening and deny-lists at password change, not just login
Conditional access with device compliance for legacy-protocol exemptions kept to zero
